title: Kartik Aaryan and Sreeleela Race to Finish Anurag Basu's Romantic Musical Before Diwali
excerpt: The untitled film — featuring music by Pritam and Arijit Singh — eyes an October release to dodge Ramayana's box office dominance.
body:
• Director Anurag Basu's untitled romantic musical starring Kartik Aaryan and Sreeleela is on track for a late 2026 release, with shooting in Srinagar, Pahalgam, Manali, and Chalsa.
  • Producer Bhushan Kumar confirmed the film is not Aashiqui 3 and is eyeing an October release to avoid clashing with Ramayana: Part 1 at Diwali.
  • Music composer Pritam has delivered what Kumar calls "outstanding" music, with at least one song by Arijit Singh confirmed.
  • The film marks Telugu star Sreeleela's Hindi debut, pairing her with Kartik Aaryan for the first time.

A Musical Taking Shape Across India's Mountains

Anurag Basu's next film has been one of Bollywood's most closely watched projects since its first promo dropped in February 2025, showing Kartik Aaryan performing on stage with a guitar, singing what fans identified as "Tu Meri Zindagi Hai." Now, with shooting well underway across multiple locations, the production is pushing to wrap before the monsoon season complicates outdoor schedules.

https://x.com/BOWorldwide/status/2088278507793326576

The film has moved through Gangtok, Srinagar, Pahalgam in Jammu and Kashmir, Chalsa in West Bengal, and Manali — a geographic spread that reflects Basu's visual ambitions for the project. On set, Kartik has adopted a rugged look: long messy hair, a full beard, and layered earthy-toned outfits that mark a sharp departure from his usual polished romantic-hero image.

Not Aashiqui 3

Speculation had linked the project to the Aashiqui franchise since its announcement, but producer Bhushan Kumar put that to rest definitively. "First of all, it's not Aashiqui 3, it's an untitled film," he told Faridoon Shahryar, confirming that while the title "Tu Meri Zindagi Hai" has circulated widely, the film is a standalone musical drama.

"It's coming out fabulous, with super duper music from Pritam. He has given outstanding music this time. Outstanding. Yes, yes, for sure, Arijit Singh is singing a song."

— Bhushan Kumar, Producer, T-Series

The music is shaping up as a central selling point. Pritam's involvement — paired with at least one Arijit Singh track — positions the soundtrack as a potential commercial driver in an era where Bollywood music's cultural footprint has been shrinking.

Sreeleela's Hindi Debut

For Sreeleela, the film represents a high-stakes entry into Hindi cinema. The Telugu star, known for her dance-heavy roles in South Indian films, is being paired with one of Bollywood's most bankable leads. The combination of a South Indian star crossing over with a commercially proven Hindi actor follows the broader industry trend of cross-regional casting that has accelerated since the pan-India success of films like RRR and Pushpa.

Speaking to Variety India, Basu addressed rumors that most of the film had already been completed. "That the majority of the shooting is done is a myth. I've not shot more than 45 days for this film. The shooting has just started," he said, indicating a substantial portion remains.

The October Gambit

The release strategy is driven by one factor: Ramayana. Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part 1, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, and Yash, is expected to dominate screens during Diwali 2026. Rather than compete with that spectacle, Basu and Kumar are targeting October, when the calendar is thinner.

"Anurag and the makers want breathing space at the box office. They are aiming for a clean theatrical run without competition from a spectacle like Ramayana."

— Source close to production, via Filmfare

Kartik, meanwhile, is juggling three projects simultaneously: this film, Dharma Productions' Naagzilla, and a Kabir Khan sports drama. The plan is to complete the Basu film first, then shift fully to the Kabir Khan project while Basu locks the final cut in post-production.

What's Next

Presented by Gulshan Kumar and T-Series, the film is produced by Bhushan Kumar and Krishan Kumar. With filming in full swing and October in sight, the next milestone will be the official title announcement and a first-look campaign. For a Bollywood calendar that has been dominated by franchise sequels and spectacle films, an original romantic musical from Anurag Basu — the director behind Barfi! and Life in a Metro — could offer a different kind of draw.
